name: Side Rays
description: WebGL2 background of soft two-color light shafts fanning in from a corner or side, with optional drifting dust motes, mouse-aimed beams, and a fade-in intro.
contents: Wrapper div filling its parent with one full-size canvas rendering the rays
behavior: Fragment shader draws two blended fans of animated shafts with glow, falloff and optional sparkle dust
Beams lean toward the pointer with spring easing and a focused brighter shaft while the pointer is over the component
Intro reveal grows the light outward over about 1.6 seconds on first mount
Pauses rendering when off screen or tab hidden, resumes automatically
Reduced motion slows the animation, disables sway and mouse tracking, and skips the intro
Canvas resolution is capped by maxDevicePixelRatio and a pixel budget, resizes with the container, and recovers from WebGL context loss
Light mode switches to dark ink-style rays for light backgrounds
editableByProps: Both ray colors and how much they blend
Origin corner or side, tilt angle, spread, density, sharpness, falloff
Dust sparkle amount, mouse following and its strength, intro on or off
Render resolution cap, wrapper className and style

needsCodeEdit.change: Add more origin positions or change where the light source sits
needsCodeEdit.where: ORIGINS constant, geometryFor function and the source/heading lines in the FRAGMENT shader
reveal increment (dt / 1.6) in the frame function
stiffness and damping constants in the frame function
uColorA, uColorB uniforms and the light mix in the FRAGMENT shader

fixed: Requires WebGL2; renders nothing if unavailable or shader compile fails
Fills its parent (h-full w-full), so the parent must have a size and positioning
Wrapper is pointer-events-none and the canvas is aria-hidden, so it is purely decorative
Listens to window pointer events and document pointerleave for mouse tracking, cleaned up on unmount
Only two ray fans exist, with a fixed two-color setup
Output is transparent with premultiplied alpha; rays are drawn over whatever is behind
Heavy shader on large or high-DPI screens; pixel budget caps resolution, which may soften rays on mobile and large displays
Client component ('use client'), uses useEffect and refs
